digest.component_or_area: inbound-probe dispatch chain / binding retirement / reconciliation
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer: differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only emits when local_state entries carry jira_key, but its sole caller passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries never carry jira_key, making everything downstream unreachable in production.

Confirmed hard-deleted Jira issues are currently resurrected on a 3-pass delay (after 3x confirmed-404 note_absent calls retire the binding), contradicting the operator ruling that deleted issues should never be resurrected.

The tombstone guard prevents resurrection by checking is_retired_local before emitting outbound-create for unbound local tickets, and unretire() provides a reversible escape hatch by removing the key from both in-memory and persisted bindings-retired.json.

The dead legacy chain (_compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes, _run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch, route_inbound_probe, _apply_inbound_delete) must be removed without re-enabling the snapshot differ's field_drift and unbound_local arms, which would duplicate work already done by outbound_differ and binding_walk.
The absence-probe capability (probe_remote, SupportsAbsenceProbe, inbound_probe.py) stays dormant pending epic e369 AC5 resolution, recorded with follow-up rebar:f020-0960-2c42-4d61.
